In addition to the regulatory considerations indicated in the previous section, the following minor MTV-specific consideration (in terms of regulatory impact) is recognized: • In terms of consideration 13.4.1.4, jack-up legs may require additional minimal analysis for sites where artificial scour would affect the natural river or tidal seabed and thus critical habitat. However, it is not expected that the addition of a jack-up system would involve substantial additional regulatory assessment as they are a common and conventional method used throughout the U.S. Final Technical Report 48/57 14 BUSINESS PLAN A business plan was developed during this project to describe a preliminary approach to MTV ownership and management. It described a high-level concept of operations with respect to MTV modes of operation, user classes associated with those modes, and the support environment. The document then explored estimated costs (ownership and operation), a marketing plan, and a pricing strategy. Several case studies were included to illustrate MTV utilization costs. Upon final design, construction, and commissioning of the MTV, it will be placed in service. The MTV must be available for use in the continental U.S. or Alaska in riverine, tidal, and open ocean locations. It is expected to have a design life of at least 20 years. The MTV’s owner is expected to maintain and make available the MTV for user use for at least this design life. Costs associated with MTV ownership and operation can be allocated to users. It was assumed that any user requirements that the final MTV configuration cannot meet would be the user's responsibility, including compatibility interfaces, mooring systems or components, the Current Energy Converter (CEC), and associated equipment. Additionally, it was assumed that transport and transit costs from the MTV’s homeport to in-service locations and any regulatory authorizations, analyses, or monitoring would be the user's responsibility. It was important to establish a context for what activities incur costs to properly frame discussions and strategies of ownership and pricing/costs. Therefore, the team selected to borrow several relevant elements from a CONOPS (Concept of Operations) [18]. The format for the plan includes modes of operation, user classes and other involved personnel, and its support environment. While not all costs and uses were known, the plan intended to provide a working framework for MTV management and planning beyond design, construction, and commissioning. 14.1 Modes of Operation Eight modes of MTV operation are anticipated. A mode of operation is defined as a utilization scenario of the MTV dedicated to a particular purpose where users interact with the vessel in different ways. 1. Mobilization - The MTV is preparing for a CEC testing campaign or transport, including loading user and MTV-specific equipment and supplies in this mode. This can be at the MTV’s homeport or a port near a deployment site (away port). Personnel may be aboard during active transfer and installation. 2. Transport/Transit - In this mode, the MTV is in transit between deployment sites, homeport, or away port. No personnel are onboard
